venue.name: Echo Players Village Theatre
venue.description: ECHO Players is a volunteer community theatre company that has owned and run the Village Theatre in Qualicum Beach since 1974. It stages four mainstage plays or musicals a season, hosts the Vancouver Island Juried One Act Play Festival each November, and runs its own youth theatre plus spring and summer musical theatre camps for ages 6 to 19. The building is scent free and children under 3 are not admitted. The site publishes no school matinees, class workshops or field trip programs of any kind, so the only way a class can come is by buying tickets to a public performance.
venue.address: 110 W 2nd Ave, Qualicum Beach, BC, V9K 1S8

facility_notes.washrooms: Unfortunately, our restrooms are not wheelchair accessible.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Our theatre has the capacity for one wheelchair per performance, please contact the Box Office to book ahead by calling 250-752-3522.

restrictions: Village Theatre is a scent free building
No admission for children under 3 years
NO REFUNDS - Exchanges may incur a fee of $3.00
venue.hours_notes: The box office opens two weeks before each production. It is also open from 6 pm to 7:30 pm on performance nights and from 12:30 pm to 2 pm before Sunday matinees.
venue.seasonal_notes: The 2026 and 2027 season is The Last Frontier from 8 to 25 October 2026, A Winter Wager from 10 to 27 December 2026, an April show still to be announced from 15 April to 2 May 2027, and Little Shop of Horrors from 8 to 25 July 2027.

programs.name: Mainstage play or musical, group booking
programs.description: A public performance of one of the four mainstage shows, with a published rate for groups of ten or more of $24 per person. Single tickets are $28 for adults, $25 for seniors 65 and over and $17 for students with valid identification. The site does not say which of those rates a school or daycare group is charged, and it does not say how a group claims the group rate. Evening performances start at 7:30 pm and closing Sunday performances are matinees at 2 pm.
programs.what_children_do: Sit in the seats of a 1949 movie house that the company converted into a theatre, and watch local actors perform a play or a musical.
programs.our_note: Nothing at this theatre is written for schools. The $24 group price sits just under the $28 adult one, so it is the adult discount, while students with identification pay $17. Ask which of the two a class of children gets before you set your budget.
programs.practical_summary: Indoors with washrooms on site, though the washrooms are not step free and the theatre can take only one wheelchair per performance. Somewhere to eat, where a bus parks and how a group actually books are all unstated, so phone the box office.
programs.extra_fees_note: The $24 is per person and needs ten or more people. Single tickets are $28 for adults, $25 for seniors 65 and over and $17 for students with valid identification. There are no refunds and an exchange can cost $3.
programs.cancellation_note: NO REFUNDS - Exchanges may incur a fee of $3.00

programs.name: December family show, child ticket
programs.description: The December show is the one production of the year with a published children's price. Children 12 and under are $15 for the Christmas play only. The December 2026 show is A Winter Wager, running from 10 to 27 December, which the company describes as a modern fairy tale that adults and children alike will find themselves immersed in through music and movement.
programs.what_children_do: Sit in the theatre and watch the December show, which the company tells through music and movement as well as through speech.
programs.our_note: This is the only show all year with a child price on it, and the only one the company writes about as being for children as well as adults. Children under 3 are not let in at all, so it will not work for a toddler room.
programs.practical_summary: Indoors, and only in December. Washrooms are on site but are not step free. Somewhere to eat, where a bus parks and how a group books are all unstated.
programs.extra_fees_note: The $15 is for children 12 and under and applies to the Christmas play only. Accompanying adults pay the usual $28, or $24 each in a party of ten or more. There are no refunds and an exchange can cost $3.
programs.cancellation_note: NO REFUNDS - Exchanges may incur a fee of $3.00

images.alt: A low white theatre building on a street corner with a VILLAGE THEATRE sign above the entrance, under a clear blue sky.
Six young performers in period costume on a lit stage, one standing at the front in a long skirt and cardigan.

gaps: PRICE, AND WHOSE PRICE. This theatre publishes no school or daycare rate at all. The rate we have recorded, $24 per person for ten or more, is the discount off the $28 adult ticket, not a children's rate. Students with valid identification are $17. Nobody says which a class gets, and on a party of 25 that is a difference of $175. Settle it on the phone before you book.
The $17 student price is written as needing valid identification, which under fives and most primary children will not have. Whether it is meant for them at all is unanswered.
The $15 child price is real but narrow. It is for children 12 and under and for the Christmas play only, which in the 2026 season means A Winter Wager between 10 and 27 December.

None of the prices carry a year or a season on the box office page, so there is no way to tell from the site how current they are. The older show pages still on the site show a different set of prices, up to $32 for an adult, so the ladder does move.

How a group of ten or more actually claims the group rate is not published. The online ticket checkout is the only route the site describes, and it is not stated whether the group price is available there.
Youngest age welcomed is 3, from the building rule that children under 3 are not admitted. That rules out infant and toddler rooms.
Group size: ten or more is the minimum for the group rate. No maximum is published, and no seating capacity is published either.
Lead time: no minimum notice is published. The box office only opens two weeks before each production.
Lunch space: nothing published. Nothing about a lobby, a concession or anywhere a group could eat.
Bus parking: nothing published. The theatre is on a village high street.
Show lengths and interval times are not published, which matters for a group that has to be back for a school bell.

Accessibility is partly published and partly a problem. The theatre takes one wheelchair per performance and asks you to book it ahead, and it says plainly that its restrooms are not wheelchair accessible. Infrared listening equipment is free on request. Nothing is said about pushchairs or about a lift.
Sensory or relaxed performances are not mentioned anywhere.

The company runs four youth camps, Spring Break-a-leg for ages 6 to 12, the Summer Youth Theatre Workshop for ages 8 to 14 at $224, JuMP! for ages 6 to 12 at $200 and Teen Musical Theatre for ages 13 to 19 at $425. These are week long or three week camps that families register a child into one at a time, not something a class or a daycare can book, so they are not recorded as programs. The 2026 summer ones are marked sold out.
Theatre rentals are handled on a separate domain, thevillagetheatre.ca, which is linked from the menu. Nothing from it has been extracted because it is not this venue's own site.
Coordinates were geocoded from the published street address. The map links on the site are plain address searches with no place pin in them.

Images: neither photograph on this record carried usable alt text on the site, so both alt lines were written after opening the images and looking at them. The site publishes no photograph of the auditorium, the seating, the lobby or the parking. The social sharing image is a night time shot of the theatre in snow, so the daylight exterior from the about page was used as the main picture instead.

conflicts.note: Two of their pages give different box office days in the fortnight before a show. One says Tuesday to Friday, the other says Tuesday to Saturday. Both give 11 am to 2 pm. If you were counting on a Saturday, phone first.
